title: The Distant Archive
premise: Elodie Thackeray, an insurance investigator specializing in impossible accidents, boards the returned deep-space vessel Meridian to determine why its crew arrived decades younger than when they departed. Her audit uncovers a signal from the Distant Archive — a station at the edge of dead space that trades years of life for knowledge — and reveals that the corporation she works for has been harvesting crews to feed it. Racing a corporate kill-team to the relay that controls the Archive, Elodie must choose between destroying the Archive (and the knowledge that could save her dying sister) or preserving it and damning every crew the company will ever send. She destroys the relay, sacrificing the Archive's gift and her own stolen years, and returns home older, poorer, and finally free.
about_author: Sable Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years auditing cargo claims before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the mathematics of survival, and live somewhere with unreliable internet.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Elodie Thackeray's POV. Ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits, and Elodie has made her name pricing the impossible — until the Meridian docks with a crew thirty years younger than their manifests. Her opening audit reads like fraud, but the biometrics don't lie. Emotional beat: weary competence cracking into genuine wonder as she realizes this claim cannot be denied, only survived.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Long Return
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with interludes from Meridian captain Ivo Renner's logs. She interviews the de-aged crew, who remember the voyage in fragments — a station that shouldn't exist, contracts signed in exchange for 'extended terms.' The corporation, Halcyon Freight, orders her to classify the incident as equipment malfunction. Emotional beat: first dread, as duty and curiosity begin pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Paperwork for Miracles
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Digging through ten years of Halcyon claims, Elodie finds a pattern: eleven vanished crews, all filed as losses, all last-transmitting near the same dead-space coordinates. Her sister Mara's medical bills sit on her desk beside the evidence. Emotional beat: quiet horror — the impossible accident is a business model, and she's been its notary.

chapters.title: Ivo Remembers the Light
chapters.summary: Ivo Renner's POV, present day. The Meridian's captain recalls the Archive in full for the first time: a structure that offered knowledge for years of life, and a voice that knew his dead wife's name. He begs Elodie not to report the coordinates. Emotional beat: grief weaponized — Ivo traded thirty years to hear his wife's voice again, and would do it twice.

chapters.title: Severance
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Halcyon suspends her clearance and reassigns the Meridian case to a 'special assets' team led by Director Casimir Voss. Mara's treatment is quietly canceled — leverage, unmistakably. Emotional beat: cold fury crystallizing into resolve; Elodie steals the coordinate ledger on her way out.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She buys passage on a smuggler's tug, the Kindly Hour, captained by Dessa Okafor, who owes Elodie for a claim she once denied honestly. Voss's kill-ship shadows them out of the station. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance — Elodie learns that trust, like insurance, is a bet placed against the odds.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. Transit through dead space: no relays, no rescue, weeks of silence. Dessa and Elodie trade histories over bad coffee; Dessa lost a brother to a Halcyon 'loss event' years ago. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling in isolation — two women who price risk for a living, daring to be a risk themselves.

chapters.title: Signal at the Edge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Kindly Hour picks up the Archive's transmission — a voice offering each crew member exactly what they most lack. The engineer hears his drowned daughter; Dessa hears her brother. Ivo's log warns: it always opens with a gift. Emotional beat: temptation as horror; the signal knows them better than they know themselves.

chapters.title: What the Archive Offers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Archive's voice addresses Elodie directly: it can give Mara ten more years. All it asks is the relay codes she carries and her own years besides. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — love against duty, with the price tag itemized in a voice like her mother's.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Distance
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The kill-ship Halcyon's Mercy overtakes them; Voss offers Dessa amnesty and Elodie a promotion, revealing Halcyon has fed the Archive for decades in exchange for navigation secrets that built their empire. Emotional beat: power's banality — Voss isn't a monster, just a man balancing a ledger with lives in the margin.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Kindly Hour
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. The engineer, tempted by his daughter's voice, tries to hand the ship to Voss. Dessa and Elodie retake the tug in a bloodless, brutal standoff, and the engineer chooses the living crew over the dead. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in trust — some debts can only be settled by staying.

chapters.title: Relay Seven
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach the ancient relay at dead space's edge, the Archive's single tether. Voss's ship arrives in weapons range. Ivo, who has been fading since the Meridian, confesses he was sent to bring the Archive a new contract — his return was no accident. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as tragedy; even the miracle was a transaction.

chapters.title: The Contract in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, final log. Ivo walks the relay's spine to buy the Kindly Hour an hour of jammed signals, paying the Archive with the last of his borrowed years. He dies young, finally old enough. Emotional beat: sacrifice as quiet accounting — a man settling his own claim in full.

chapters.title: Older Than Her Years
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Boarding the Archive's outer ring to destroy the relay from inside, Elodie meets the Archive's custodian — a de-aged crewman from a vanished ship, kept as a living interface. He shows her the truth: the Archive doesn't steal years, it accepts them, and someone must always choose to feed it. Emotional beat: the corruption isn't the machine; it's the market built around it.

chapters.title: Ten Years for Mara
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Archive makes its final offer, live: Mara's decade, itemized against Elodie's remaining years, the relay codes, and the Kindly Hour's silence. Elodie's hand is on the acceptance plate. Emotional beat: the lowest point — love against duty, and duty losing, until she remembers Voss waiting outside to own whatever she buys.

chapters.title: What Voss Buys
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss boards to secure the Archive for Halcyon, planning to monetize the trade at scale — fleets of crews, years by the ton. He offers Elodie partnership and, when she refuses, orders the Kindly Hour destroyed. Emotional beat: power completing its arc from pragmatism to atrocity, all with a signature and a smile.

chapters.title: Burn the Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie and Dessa's alternating POV. Elodie triggers the relay's overload from inside while Dessa flies the Kindly Hour straight through Voss's firing solution to buy her seconds. The Archive screams in a thousand borrowed voices as the tether burns. Emotional beat: climax — love against duty resolved by refusing the terms entirely; the price of survival is finally naming what isn't for sale.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Impossible
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. The relay dies; the Archive goes dark and unreachable. Voss's ship limps away, his career and his cargo of secrets ash. The Kindly Hour drifts, damaged, with a decade of Elodie's life unspent and unrecoverable. Emotional beat: hollow victory — survival that feels like amputation, and the first honest silence in years.

chapters.title: Claims Adjusted
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Home again, Elodie files her final report with Halcyon: eleven vanished crews, one director, one Archive, all losses. She leaks the ledger publicly and lets the industry eat itself. Mara's treatment is funded by the bounty on Voss. Emotional beat: justice as paperwork — the weapon she was given is the one that ends it.

chapters.title: The Years She Kept
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Mara, stabilizing, asks what it cost. Elodie can't answer in numbers. She returns to the Kindly Hour not as an investigator but as crew, signing on for a run with no claim to file and nothing to price. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin — learning to live unmeasured.

chapters.title: A Signal, Faint
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. At dead space's edge, a whisper persists where the relay stood — not the Archive, but something answering it, patient, listening. Dessa logs it and, after a long moment, does not report it. Emotional beat: ambiguous grace — some doors, once opened, never fully close.

chapters.title: The Distant Archive
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, coda. Years later, older now on purpose, Elodie teaches investigators to ask not just what a loss costs, but who profits from the pricing. She keeps Ivo's final log and reads it aloud each year to the crew of the Kindly Hour. Emotional beat: resolution — the Archive is gone, but the choice it offered lives in everyone; she chose the years she had, and calls them enough.
